sections.name: THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF PENNSYLVANIA
sentences: CASE MANAGEMENT TRACK DESIGNATION FORM.

In accordance with the Civil Justice Expense and Delay Reduction Plan of this court, counsel for plaintiff shall complete a Case Management Track Designation Form in all civil cases at the time of filing the complaint and serve a copy on all defendants. (See § 1:03 of the plan set forth on the reverse side of this form.) In the event that a defendant does not agree with the plaintiff regarding said designation, that defendant shall, with its first appearance, submit to the clerk of court and serve on the plaintiff and all other parties, a Case Management Track Designation Form specifying the track to which that defendant believes the case should be assigned. (a) Habeas Corpus – Cases brought under 28 U.S.C. § 2241 through § 2255. ( ) (b) Social Security – Cases requesting review of a decision of the Secretary of Health and Human Services denying plaintiff Social Security Benefits. ( ) (c) Arbitration – Cases required to be designated for arbitration under Local Civil Rule 53.2. ( ) (d) Asbestos – Cases involving claims for personal injury or property damage from exposure to asbestos. ( ) (e) Special Management – Cases that do not fall into tracks (a) through (d) that are commonly referred to as complex and that need special or intense management by the court. (See reverse side of this form for a detailed explanation of special management cases.) ( ) (f) Standard Management – Cases that do not fall into any one of the other tracks. (x ) 12/17/2020 Graham F. Baird Gregory Priester Date Attorney-at-law Attorney for 267-546-0131 215-944-6124 GrahamB@ericshore.com Telephone FAX Number E-Mail Address (Civ.
Parties and Reasons for Jurisdiction.
Plaintiff, GREGORY PRIESTER (hereinafter “Plaintiff”) is an adult individual residing at the above address.

Defendant, VALLEY YOUTH HOUSE (hereinafter “Defendant”), is a corporation organized by and operating under the laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and having a corporate headquarters at the above captioned address.
At all times material hereto, Defendant qualifies as Plaintiff’s employers pursuant to the Title VII of the Civil Rights Act and the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act (“PHRA”).

Plaintiff has exhausted his administrative remedies pursuant to the Equal Employment Opportunity Act and the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act. (See Exhibit A, a true and correct copy of a “right-to-sue” letter issued by the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission.) This action is instituted pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act and applicable federal law. Jurisdiction is conferred by 28 U.S.C. §§ 1331 and 1343.
Supplemental jurisdiction over the Plaintiff’s state law claims is conferred pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1367.

Pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b)(1) and (b)(2), venue is properly laid in this district because Defendant conducts business in this district, and because a substantial part of the acts and/or omissions giving rise to the claims set forth herein occurred in this judicial district.
Plaintiff was working in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania at the time of the illegal actions by Defendant as set forth herein.

sections.name: Operative Facts.
sentences: Plaintiff is an African American male.
On or about January 21, 2019, Plaintiff was hired by Defendant as a maintenance worker at Defendant’s Achieving Independence Center located at 1415 N. Broad Street, Suite 100, Philadelphia, PA 19122.
At all times material hereto, Plaintiff was the only African-American employee in his department, with all of his co-workers being Caucasian.

Beginning in June of 2019, Plaintiff began to be subjected to racial harassment on behalf of Defendant’s supervisor, Fran Haar, a Caucasian man. Mr. Haar stated to Plaintiff, “All you niggers are hard-headed.” Plaintiff made a complaint to Defendant’s regional supervisor Gus Warren, a Caucasian man, regarding the harassment.
Mr. White stated he would “talk to Mr. Haar”; however, Mr. Haar’s behavior toward Plaintiff did not change.

Mr. Haar continued to speak abusively toward Plaintiff and use racial slurs, including the “n word.” Plaintiff lodged several more complaints with HR regarding Mr. Haar but nothing was done to address Mr. Haar’s conduct.
On or about September 26, 2019, Mr. Haar confronted Plaintiff regarding a work issue.
During this encounter, Mr. Haar again said to Plaintiff, “All you niggers are hard- headed.” Plaintiff told Mr. Haar not to say that to him again.
Mr. Haar repeated the statement, and also stated “You niggers never listen”, and Plaintiff left the office.
Later that day, Plaintiff was summoned to a meeting with Defendant’s Human Resources department.

Plaintiff spoke with Defendant’s Human Resources representative, Sherice, who indicated that Mr. Haar stated that Plaintiff had “threatened” him. Plaintiff explained what had happened and what Mr. Haar said, but was sent home.
On September 27, 2019, Plaintiff was informed his employment was being terminated for “threatening” his supervisor.

Defendant’s explanation to Plaintiff concerning the reason for his termination was untrue pretext and discriminatory retaliation towards Plaintiff for lodging his race discrimination complaints against Mr. Haar.
Mr. Haar’s behavior was never addressed even after Plaintiff made several complaints regarding the harassing and discriminatory manner in which he was being treated.
III. Causes of Action.

sections.name: COUNT I – EMPLOYMENT DISCRIMINATION
sentences: (42 U.S.C.A. § 2000e-2(a)) Plaintiff incorporates paragraphs 1-26 as if fully set forth at length herein.
Defendant took adverse action against Plaintiff by terminating his employment.
Plaintiff’s race was a motivating factor in Defendant’s decision to terminate his employment.
Plaintiff was subjected to a hostile work environment by Defendant, as set forth above.
As such, Defendant’s decision to terminate Plaintiff’s employment is an unlawful employment practice, under 42. U.S.C. § 2000e-2(a).

As a proximate result of Defendant’s conduct, Plaintiff sustained significant damages, including but not limited to: great economic loss, future lost earning capacity, lost opportunity, loss of future wages, loss of front pay, loss of back pay, as well as emotional distress, mental anguish, humiliation, pain and suffering, consequential damages and Plaintiff has also sustained work loss, loss of opportunity, and a permanent diminution of earning power and capacity and a claim is made therefore.
As a result of the conduct of Defendant’s owners/management, Plaintiff hereby demands punitive damages.
Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, 42 U.S.C. §2000e-2(a), et seq Plaintiff demands attorneys fees and court costs.

sections.name: COUNT II – TITLE VII CLAIM--RETALIATION
sentences: (42 U.S.C.A. § 2000e-3(a)) Plaintiff incorporates paragraphs 1-34 as if fully set forth at length herein.

At set forth above, Plaintiff attempted to complain about racial discrimination in the workplace and as such, Plaintiff was engaged in protected activity under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act. Defendant took adverse action against Plaintiff by terminating his employment.
As set forth above, Plaintiff’s participation in protected activity was a motivating factor in Defendant’s decision to terminate his employment.
As such, Defendant’s decision to terminate Plaintiff’s employment is a retaliatory action prohibited by the Civil Rights Act of 1964, § 704(a).

As a proximate result of Defendant’s conduct, Plaintiff sustained significant damages, including but not limited to: great economic loss, future lost earning capacity, lost opportunity, loss of future wages, loss of front pay, loss of back pay, as well as emotional distress, mental anguish, humiliation, pain and suffering, consequential damages and Plaintiff also sustained work loss, loss of opportunity, and a permanent diminution of earning power and capacity and a claim is made therefore.
As a result of the conduct of Defendant’s owners/management, Plaintiff hereby demands punitive damages.
Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, § 704(a), 42 U.S.C. §2000e-3(a), et seq., Plaintiff demands attorneys fees and court costs.

sections.name: (43 P.S. § 955)
sentences: Plaintiffs incorporate paragraphs 1-42 as if fully set forth at length herein.
At all times material hereto, and pursuant to the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, 43 P.S. § 951, et seq,, an employer may not discriminate against an employee.
Plaintiff is a qualified employee and person within the definition of Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, 43 P.S. § 951, et seq,.
Defendant is an “employer” and is thereby subject to the strictures of the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, 43 P.S. § 951, et seq,.
Defendant’s conduct in terminating Plaintiff is an adverse action, was taken as a result of his race and constitutes a violation of the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, 43 P.S. § 951, et seq,.

Defendant’s aforementioned conduct in terminating Plaintiff’s employment constitutes an adverse action and was taken as a result of his complaints and/or opposition concerning the disparate treatment of his Caucasian co-workers which constitutes a violation of the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, 43 P.S. § 951, et seq,.

As a proximate result of Defendant’s conduct, Plaintiff sustained significant damages, including but not limited to: great economic loss, future lost earning capacity, lost opportunity, loss of future wages, loss of front pay, loss of back pay, loss of tips as well as personal injury, emotional distress, mental anguish, humiliation, pain and suffering, consequential damages and Plaintiff has also sustained work loss, loss of opportunity, and a permanent diminution of his earning power and capacity and a claim is made therefore.
Pursuant to the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, 43 P.S. § 951, et seq Plaintiff demands attorney’s fees and court costs.

sections.name: Relief Requested.
sentences: WHEREFORE, Plaintiff GREGORY PRIESTER demands judgment in his favor and against Defendant, VALLEY YOUTH HOUSE jointly and severally, in an amount in excess of $150,000.00 together with: Compensatory damages, including but not limited to: back pay, front pay, past lost wages, future lost wages.

Lost pay increases, lost pay incentives, lost opportunity, lost benefits, lost future earning capacity, injury to reputation, mental and emotional distress, pain and suffering and personal injury damages; Punitive damages; Attorneys fees and costs of suit; Interest, delay damages; and, Any other further relief this Court deems just proper and equitable.
